Travel Yoga Mat, Foldable Thin Mats for Travelling, Bonus Folding Light Pad and Strap for Hot Yoga, Pilates Floor Exercise Fitness Dancing (2-2.8 lbs) I got this mainly for my wife, but I also do the p90x Yoga routine and know the value of a good mat. I liked this mat design better than the typical rolls you see people carrying around. Those rolls tend to curl up at the ends which gets pretty annoying and is a distraction from what you're trying to achieve. This mat lays absolutely flat and is easy to clean (hand wash, don't put it in the washing machine).

The surface has a good grip and you feel very stable whether you use it with bare feet or socks. It's not as thick as a typical mat, but it is very large and you can fold it up on itself if you need extra padding. The product measures 70 inches by 24 inches and comes in an attractive box that makes this an ideal gift.

Also, it's small enough to fit in a backpack, so you don't have to carry around a huge rolled up tube. Finally, it doesn't pick up odors even with regular use.

The product description says "towel" mat, but this is not really a towel. One side of the mat has a kind of rubbery, grip surface, and the other side feels like a dense knit cloth, but you wouldn't want to try to dry yourself off with this. It's thick enough that it would prevent sticks from poking through the mat.

For anyone who doesn't like normal Yoga mats, this is an innovative and effective design that is sanitary and built to last.

text_fidelity_a:
Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe I am adding this paragraph after three trips. The bindings have lots of rivets, and
I wondered about their durability. After the third trip, when I took off the shoes,
one of the rivets holding the heel strap broke. Fortunately I was back at the car;
if some of the rivets fail out on the trail, the shoe could become useless. Other
reviews that I have seen have not mentioned a problem with durability, but now I
wonder. The rest of the review hasn't changed.

This snowshoe has lots of good points. The only negative, and the reason that I did
not give it 5 stars, is a lack of flotation. I cannot compare it to other snowshoes
of the "modern" solid decking type, or the "traditional" wood frame lattice decking,
though it seems to have less flotation than my traditional shoes. I got the 27"
model, and with pack I weigh under 165 lbs; the shoes are rated to 200 lbs or more.
In a soft, old snow, I sank in 8-12" breaking trail; sometimes I sank in more.

The shoe has some very good points. The bindings are secure and comfortable, and
they won't ruin your leather boots or give you blisters by clamping down on the top
of your toes. The traction is good. The toes snap up automatically, and you can walk
with a pretty normal stride. Because of the short distance between your toes and
the toes of the shoes, the lack of a long tail, and the crampons, you can climb
over deadfall very easily. There's no need to back up to free your toes, burying
your tail in the process. I like the heel lift, though I only tried it briefly.
The lift bars are very stiff to put back down. The shoes are lightweight and don't
carry lots of snow on their tops, so you don't have to lift lots of weight with
each step. The natural stride and light weight tend to offset the less than ideal
flotation.

Pros:
Excellent binding system, excellent or very good traction, very good walking
stride, light weight

Cons:
Flotation may be somewhat lacking - I can't compare to other shoes, just to an
ideal, which is not possible to achieve
text_fidelity_b: Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe

Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver If you take the time to research the product, regardless of who markets it, you will find that citronella, as a mosquito repellent, does not, will not, CAN NOT do what it is advertised to do.
The best mosquito repellent is a slight breeze. These insects have extreme difficulty flying/navigating in the slightest breeze.

The reason you see dead mosquitoes in the wax, flame (or light of most types) attracts them. When they fly into the flame, wings, antennaeI, and proboscis get burned off. They fall into the hot wax, and die.

I buy these, locally, to use while fishing. Buy only for the light provided.
To sum it up: people have been told, for decades, that citronella repels mosquitoes, they are persuaded that it works, not noticing a slight breeze, in stead it’s, “Oh, my word! This stuff works!!!”
Do some research. Read a bit. And save your money.
Type in your search engine: how citronella works.
Be amazed !!!
text_fidelity_b: Cutter 66384 Camping-Candles, pack of 1, silver

TANGCISON Fishing Hat, Sun Hat with Face&Neck Flap, UPF 50+ Womens/Mens Sun Protection Cap for Camping Hiking The TANGCISON Sun Hat is definitely a cooler option than the sun protection hoodies I’ve been wearing outside this summer. And by cooler, I mean temperature-wise. Not stylistically; I look like a dork when I wear the hat with the mesh snapped on, but I don’t care.

The hat itself is lightweight, comfortable, and breathable. The brim really does fold so you can stuff the hat in a bag without it taking up a lot of space. I was worried the brim wouldn’t be stable when wearing the hat, but the fold lines actually help the brim curve and provide better light blocking.

The hat is not adjustable in the normal sense, you can’t make it tighter. The back band is elastic, not a sliding buckle.

The mesh portion to protect the face and back of the neck is somewhat flimsy, and honestly, I am worried how much sun it actually blocks. The mesh is transparent, I can see my face underneath it. So I still put on sunscreen.

I did discover the mesh portion can be stuffed inside the hat and I can still wear the hat on my head. So if I needed the mesh and then didn’t need it, I can just hide it away in the hat and not worry about losing or unsnapping it.

text_fidelity_a:
Mongoose Trace Youth Kick Scooter Folding and Non-Folding Design, Regular, Lighted, and Air Filled Wheels, Multiple Colors I'm a 5'8" tall adult weighing about 170 lbs. This scooter with the air filled 12" tires is to replace another scooter I use to ride along with my grandkids. A scooter with smaller hard rubber wheels is hazardous when the sidewalk is uneven. Tree roots often push up part of a sidewalk, and a 1" difference in elevation is not fun. The more you weigh, the more difficult it is for the wheels to "make the jump." My other scooter also had a rear disc brake which is very nice.
As an adult, I found it difficult to find a kick scooter with big wheels and hand brakes tall enough for an adult. After much research, I chose this Mongoose.
I've been maintaining my own bicycles since the 1970s. One would think a scooter is a piece of cake to assemble! And it should be...except it's not!
This scooter is sturdy, nicely painted, the wheels are nice, although I would have preferred a slightly taller handlebar. The difficulty is with the caliper brakes.
The instruction manual points out how the left brake handle is for the front, and the right one is for the rear. So far so good. However, the actual hardware appears to want to accommodate both breaks from either handle.
Being made in China, maybe the Chinese do it differently. But Mongoose literature says they hail from Madison Wisconsin.
So, I've about finished with the front brake. After I removed a "double cable" and stretched the proper cable to the handlebar brake lever. However, the rear brake cable also has a "double cable" and the single cable from the rear caliper is not long enough to reach the right brake lever.
I shall try and contact the manufacturer tomorrow. Lucky for me, I happen to have a collection of brake cables from my years of home bicycle maintenance to make it work. But I should not have to do that.
Hopefully, Mongoose will get together with their Chinese manufacturer and straighten this out for future buyers. Might I suggest they move their manufacturing to Wisconsin where they hail from. They might also consider revising their instruction manual for more clarity.
ADULT USER UPDATE:
I've come to find out that this is a "Trick Scooter" as in circus. The twin rear brake cables allow for the handlebars to spin in 360 degree circles while "riding." I don't expect to use the scooter in this fashion.
Customer service was friendly and attentive. They shipped me a missing lock nut (in the mail) and noted by observations about the brakes. Although the brakes are fully adjusted, they require an unusual amount of hand gripping force to lock the wheels. I believe this is because the length of the caliper arms from the pivot point to the rim pads is exceptionally long. In my opinion, it is a design issue. There is a wide gap between the top of the tire and the single mounting point of the brake calipers. Therefore, the mechanical advantage to stop the wheels from spinning is very weak. This problem is compounded with speed and the weight of an adult rider. I would not ride this scooter on a steep hill. I believe a rear wheel disc brake would be a fine solution. That, or modify the frame design to enable installation of high leverage rim brakes.

As my purpose is ride and supervise young grandchildren and riding on mostly level sidewalks at low speeds, I will probably keep this scooter despite its shortcomings. But I should not have to settle for this due to lack of choice. An adult kick scooter with 12" pneumatic wheels and hand brakes without an electric motor is difficult to find.
text_fidelity_b: Mongoose Trace Youth Kick Scooter Folding and Non-Folding Design, Regular, Lighted, and Air Filled Wheels, Multiple Colors

text_fidelity_a:
SUGARBEAR'S Smart Weighted Hula Hoop Corset Waist Trimmer Waist Trainer Fitness Workout Plus Size Pop It Fidget (One Size, Smart Weighted Hula Hoop) This is the first “smart” weighted hula hoop I’ve used, so I can’t compare it first-hand to others, but I can say that I found this one very difficult to use. First off, I feel the product description is misleading. It states “24 detachable parts” which is correct, but that doesn’t mean 24 separate sections as I think is the case with most of these types of hula hoops. After doing some reading about other models, it seems most have 24 sections meaning it’s possible to customize the waist band to best fit your body. With this hula hoop, there are only 2 large sections and 5 additional, smaller sections. The smaller sections are 5”, so there’s no adjusting by a just a couple of inches. For me, that didn’t work. With an extra section added, the hula hoop was too big and tended to move around too much on my waist and end up at an angle rather than parallel with the floor. With a section taken out, it was too tight. There was no middle ground to fit me. And as far as adding and removing sections, it’s not easy. The pieces are difficult to get into place, and even more difficult to open back up. The sections snap together, then there are white pins that hold them together (these count for some of the advertised 24 pieces). The pins are very difficult to put in and take out, especially when the hula hoop is around your waist. The weight on this hula hoop is just a flimsy plastic bottle with a screw top that you need to fill with water or sand. The bottle arrived partially crushed, it was difficult to pop it back into shape, and when I filled it with water and secured the cap, it still leaked sending occasional drops of water flying. It’s up to the user to tie a knot to secure the rope on the end of the weight meaning the possibility exists the knot comes loose and the weight sails across the room. Other hula hoops I looked at have a clip to attach the weight. The hula hoop has a counter that keeps track of revolutions which is nice, but again, it appears other brands have trackers that do more and provide more options to monitor your workout.
Overall, the hula hoop does work, but it’s not very customizable and not very user friendly.
text_fidelity_b: SUGARBEAR'S Smart Weighted Hula Hoop Corset Waist Trimmer Waist Trainer Fitness Workout Plus Size Pop It Fidget (One Size, Smart Weighted Hula Hoop)

Pelican 7060 Rechargeable Tactical Flashlight With Charger (Black) I bought two of these 8 years ago and they're still functioning perfectly. Back then we were living in a coyote infested area of Arizona, and the concentrated beam and distance these lights put out allowed me to scan the perimeter of the back yard and surrounding area for coyotes to protect my pet dogs when I took them out at night.

We've since moved to a rural area of Texas and the lights are still my favorites because sometimes I have to go outside in the dark to turn off a septic system alarm or take the dogs out, and I'll grab one of these to take with to light my way as well as check the meadows and woods around for anything out there.

With the distance the light beam penetrates I think I'll be able to spot "red eyes" of any predators, and if not at least I can blind anything that gets too close long enough to make it safely back to my door. I also feel better knowing that this flashlight is long and sturdy enough for me to use it for self defense in certain situations as well. The 7060 isn't inexpensive, but it's proven it's worth to me time after time, and it's still going strong. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it - and in fact, I think I'm going to invest in one more this year to position in another spot in the house as well.

CHECK to make sure it SPRAYS from time to time. Like hair spray, after awhile, even if there is some left, it may not spray. You don't want to find this out when you need it.

IF a dog is coming at you in an aggressive manner, TRY just spraying in front of you before the dog is too near. I did this once with a dog running at me, and as soon as he got a whiff of this, he turned around and ran the other way. I didn't even have to spray him directly. IF AN ANIMAL OR HUMAN IS WAY TOO CLOSE and you are about to be attacked, SPRAY BACK AND FORTH AND AIM FOR EYES, NOSE.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan This 10" pre-seasoned cast iron grill pan by Coleman was offered at a very economical price as compared to similar items and meets the needs for which I intended to use it just fine. I needed a safe surface to do the final searing of sous vide steaks, chops and chicken for two so this is safe enough to handle the high intensity heat of the blow torch I use and sized is just right for a couple of steaks, chops, or chicken breasts at a time.

The sides are high enough to prevent my searing flame from flowing over the item and out of the pan area, the ribs contain the juices, and the pour spout makes draining easy. The handle is also cast iron so bear in mind that you need to wear oven mitts to protect your hands when cooking in the pan since it will get hot.

This pan is pre-seasoned, but that doesn't mean exactly the same thing as a non-stick coating. When it comes to cast iron pans, seasoning means a vegetable oil baked onto the iron at a high temperature which serves to protect the cast iron from moisture which would lead to the pan rusting, and also serves as a natural non-stick film for easy release of the item you're cooking.

You might want to add a little butter or oil if you're cooking eggs in the new pan however since the best non-stick benefits of seasoning haven't had a chance to really build up yet. After using this pan you should hand wash it, dry it completely, and then rub it with a light coating of vegetable oil on it to restore a sheen.

The more you use the pan and re-season it the better the non-stick tendency will be, and that's why a lot of folks love finding old cast iron pans at yard sales. Those old pans that were lovingly used & cared for over a long time had years to get well seasoned. If you take care of this one it should serve you well over the years so I'd gladly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan

Really thick gel that's the perfect cushion for my ROCK HARD bike seat. It appears very well made and comes with a "rain hat" to cover it.

I've comandeered my mountain bike to use as an exerbike during the pandemic year. I put that bike on a Wahoo KICKR, hooked it up to FulGaz virtual rides, pulled on my padded Pearl Izumi bike shorts and..... got EXCRUTIATING sciatica down my right leg for several weeks! I think it's cuz my ROCK HARD bike seat was killing that nerve as I ground away the miles. There's no other exercise I've done that would cause the sciatica. Once I got that painful issue under control with physical therapy, I got right back on the exerbike - but riding on this Zacro gel seat!

All I did is set the gel seat on top of my old bike seat and tie the straps it comes with in a square knot under the front end of my old bike seat; the back of the gel seat secures with a very effective drawstring to hold it snugly to the old bike seat. Took no more than 30 seconds to put it on! The seat does NOT wiggle, slide or shift out of position in a good 10-mi (50 min) ride. I have not had a single sciatica incident since using this gel seat, so I'm HOPING that took care of the problem.

Highly recommend this very practical, well-made gel seat cover for anyone who lacks padding where it counts and wants a comfortable ride.

The controls for this desk could use some improvements. You have to hold down the stop button for a few seconds before you can power off the device, which is stupid and unintuitive for such a frequent action.

They should come up with a better way to lubricate the tread since that is routine maintenance. I cannot lift up one side of the tread at all since it is not centered on mine and the lubrication tube on my bottle is not long enough to reach the other side. I have no effective way of lubricating half of the tread.

Another improvement would be a dust collector for all the debris that falls off and collects at the back of the treadmill portion.

Overall this could use many improvements. However, these products are still relatively new and the competition does not have these problems solved either. Looking at the treadmill desks available for sale, this is a good one, even with the flaws.

Update: I ended up removing the console to use on a better desk and it worked without having to cut wires. I was able to pry off the hole covers and angle the wire connector through the holes in the desk leg to remove the long wire from the desk. I left the shorter wires in place for now. Before pulling the wire down through the desk leg I attached twine to it so that the wire in the leg is replace with twine. This allows me to pull the wire back up through the desk leg if I want to restore the original Lifespan desk. I am trying out an Ikea standing desk that is easier to adjust the height of and it has a bigger surface area. The markings on the long wire are: E146924 AWM I/II A/B 24AWG VW-1 300V. I looked for a replacement wire that I could buy and could not find one pre-made.

Update: this Ikea desk has been working great. It is much better than the supplied LifeSpan desk because I can lower the height if I want to sit down with the Ikea desk. The Ikea desk does not wobble at the highest setting. I am 6' 1".
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan TR1200-DT5 Treadmill Desk

text_fidelity_a:
MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone I fully admit, we got this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag for our two unknown/lesser known brand eScooters not knowing if we had a chance for it to fit. It is not one of the ones listed on the product page, so... in the end, it has worked out great on both our eScooters, so we are happy to have it.

This MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag has two straps at the top to go on the handlebars, two on the back to wrap and hold it to the upright stick of the eScooter. But would there be enough room between/around/next too the break and accelerator? For both of ours, yes. They fit slightly differently, but yes, we got them on there, no problem. The straps on the back - one over the other - holds the bag to the stick perfectly. The top ones come with such a long piece of material, you have various options on length down the front stick - we can actually do it at varying heights and simply wrap the remaining material. The ones on the back are a little more limited, but not so much that we could not also adjust - here it was how tight to make it against the stick, and this varied by how high or low we did the top one. In other words, there is enough material on the top two straps that it allowed us to adjust the placement of the bag on the two different eScooters, and on each eScooter itself, for more overall options.

The bag is a good size. We can get both wallets, a phone or two, keys, all in there. The velcro holds it strong enough. And we are good to go. We do NOT ride in any weather, so no idea how it would handle rain - but we never want to find out. We THINK it would be okay and keep stuff good. There is a solid, type material for the shell, cloth for the edges, all SHOULD hold back the rain - but that cloth COULD potentially get soaked and leaked. But our understanding of eScooters - you'd have a bigger problem with the scooter getting wet first.

In the end we are thrilled with this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag and while we are using it on our eScooters, we feel it would go on a bike or other item as well, depending on the design of course, but opens more options for using it. We're thrilled.
text_fidelity_b: MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone

I am a petite lady and I was able to put this tent up by myself (only took 25 min from box to erect, while stopping to look at the directions) it is a very heavy tent, but I was able to put it up with a bit of effort.
Once up I was able to really get a look at this tent... WOW! This tent is large and heavy duty! The floor is a thick rubber-like material that you can tell isn't gonna leak (and it didn't, even when there were puddles of rain water between the tarp below and tent) I sprayed the tent down (as per directions) prior to our first camping trip. And off we went...
This tent has turned heads every time we camp, it is a heavy duty, quality tent that we know will last for years to come... It is so simple to put up, and we are so pleased with our investment.
We have not yet had it stand the test of a storm, but I have no doubt it will hold up well.
As far as staying warm, the larger tent makes it difficult to stay warm, so bundle up and use warm blankets ;)

Oh, did I mention the tent storage bag?!?! It's awesome, and your tent will always fit, no need for super tight refilling to make it fit in the bag, this bag adjusts and will always fit your rolled up tent (we fold in half, then half again, roll and adjust the bag to fit )

To summarize:
Pros:
Large roomy tent that you can stand and walk around in, the walls are straight so you don't lose storage room
Durable canvas that is waterproof
Quality thick floor that will not leak
Heavy duty metal rods/poles and steaks
Large doors and windows makes the tent feel even more open and allows a cross breeze
The ingenious tent bag that will always be able to fit the tent once rolled up

Cons:
The long poles (when storing) and the weight of the tent
No electrical slot for extension cords (have to put them through the door)

Overall If you are in the market for a quality tent that will last for years to come...buy this tent!

Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black If you have the type of seat post where the saddle rails are sandwiched/clamped between two contoured plates this saddle might not work on your seat post clamp. This saddle comes with one of those rotary, rotating, claw-type clamps and the saddle likely works fine with that included clamp. However better bike seat posts can't use the included claw clamp type -- they must use their own sandwich-type. Technically, this saddle still should still mount but the distance between the rails was too wide. If you are confused about the difference do a web search for 'bike seat rail clamp' and you'll see the two different families of clamps.

I would have thought that the measured distance between saddle rails would be standardized but the rails on this saddle were just a very few millimeters too wide for both my sandwich-type clamps (it failed to mount on the two different seat post clamps I tried it on). The distance could maybe be lessened by clamping the rails, in a vice, for example, or using some other tool but I decided to return it rather than mess with it..

Otherwise it seemed okay, maybe quite a bit on the stiff side for a gel saddle.

text_fidelity_a:
Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz I do like having these bottles for bikepacking. It makes the difference between having to carry some kind of bladder vs making the jump between towns in the middle of summer during midday. The 1L capacity is the big appeal for me.

For me, the Camelback Podium water bottles are the best I've used. I would rate the Podium at 4 stars. I've gotten used to the annoyances and now I have really on positive associations with that water bottle .

This Zefal bottle gets additional points for capacity, and loses many points for the following criteria:
Distinct plastic taste that appears very quickly. With my other water bottles, I detect some leeching only when I leave water in the bottle overnight or longer. With the Zefal, it's almost immediate. That worries me.

Requires too much force to seal the lid. On my first bikepacking trip with these, I kept wasting water because my first squeeze after each stop would go on my face and jersey, in addition to my mouth. I'm used to it now and I know how hard I need to muscle on the lids.

No jet nozzle. This is the same basic design as water bottles had 40 years ago. It's not horrible - it works like it's supposed to; OTOH if the Camelback is 4 stars then this design is worth much less.

Branding: I simply feel strange about branding on really low-end items. IDK - maybe I'm afraid that people with think that I think this is great water bottle? Maybe I shouldn't take that out on the product. I definitely don't mind the Camelback logo, no matter how outlandish and counter to my design taste, and yet with these bottles even the conservative branding seems to be in bad taste.

Overall, this bottle simply fails to meet my criterion for good cycling gear: its interface/use is not transparent. I.e. instead of simply using it routinely / out of habit / on muscle memory, I'm always aware of opening the valve, tasting plastic, and remembering to close the valve as I return it to the cage. Gear that I consider over the threshold for good sinks down out of sight much faster than my habit formation with these - assuming I will ever get used to them. At this point it seems more likely that next summer I'll set out of find a better solution to this same problem.

I simply don't like these bottles.

Overall this feels like many levels of quality down from the Camelback bottles. I find the capacity appealing and really nothing else. It's like the quip about cookie-cutter, drywall box "McMansion": it's not home, but it's much.
text_fidelity_b: Zefal 164 Water Bottle, 33 oz

text_fidelity_a:
YOOHO 4 Piece Kayak Paddles for Adult with Comfort Grips Adjuatable Kayak Oars for Easy to Carry and Store Perfect for Kayaking Boating 91.8in/230cm Aluminum Shaft PP Blade My wife and I enjoy kayaking and she enjoys SUPing - my ankles are not strong enough and while I do it, I tend to end up sitting longer than standing. To that end I grabbed these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles to take instead of a SUP paddle with my new SUP. A couple things: 1. we have done both kayaking and SUPing, but always in a group, so we are new at having our own and beginners with limited knowledge of what is good vs. not. This is all presented from that beginners perspective. 2. While we have new SUPs and paddles, we are not able to get out for several more weeks. Between a very rainy year so far in 2021 and my recent major surgery limiting what I can do, we are getting these as a promise to ourselves and with an eye to being back out and active as soon as possible. Therefore, this review is also from having and using the paddle out of the water.

Having read about paddles and having used them in a limited way, I do find that these YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddles are a big heavier - I’ve held lighter. But it’s fine for my needs. We will get out there several times a year on salt water (mostly intercostal) and we feel this will be a good set for the setting and our ability level. It looks nice - I like the blue and black - and the materials seem solid. That said, I cannot give this a 5 star rating - it only deserves 4 stars in that putting it together - while easy - was hindered by a peg that was/is not exactly spot on. As you can see in the pics, one button went in well - easy on the first try - on both ends. The other one does not. I tried it first actually, placing it in, getting it lined up, but it is JUST-THAT-OFF (short) that it would not pop out. I tried the other end. It also did not pop out. As I am recovering from surgery I was not able to “fight it’ and had my wife. She was finally - after much effort - able to fight in into one end where it would pop out securing it into place by the pop out. Because of this 1. It’s far harder to set in place that is should and 2. makes us question it’s strength when in use. Would it too easily pop out? So to that end, 4 stars. They need to do better on lining up those pegs that keep the ends in place. It seems like a great paddle, but it needs to get together and apart quickly, easily, and stay together safely. This YOOHO Kayak Paddle with Comfort Grips 4 Piece Adjuatable Paddle set is not good enough to say it does that.
text_fidelity_b: YOOHO 4 Piece Kayak Paddles for Adult with Comfort Grips Adjuatable Kayak Oars for Easy to Carry and Store Perfect for Kayaking Boating 91.8in/230cm Aluminum Shaft PP Blade

Franklin Sports Anywhere Darts - Double-Sided Dart Target Hangs Anywhere - Perfect for Kids and Families We like to have fun in the office but unfortunately there are certain things we cannot have there, like a real dart board mounted on the wall. I chose this set as the solution to that problem. It’s a little bit different than regular darts but it’s still a lot of fun and it meets the safety requirements that are in place there.

This kind of set has been around for a while – felt-like board, velcro-lined balls. It comes down to how well your aim is when tossing or throwing the balls. The target is set up a bit differently than a traditional dart board and is more in line with what kids would play, but that’s the point – it’s suitable for kids as well as adults, and can be played anywhere. The target has two sides, one with point zones more similar to a traditional board (but still very different) and the other side has point circles as well as “lose” circles. Depending on what mood your group is in, either is suitable for a quick game.

This is a very lightweight and portable game. It packs easily and doesn’t take up much room in luggage. It would have been nice to have a carry bag with it, even if it was just a nylon baggie that does little more than keep everything together.

I have not used the hanging hook. I have found different ways to hang the target.

This is a fun and easy game that can be played almost anywhere and doesn’t require a lot of thought. It’s easy to understand, easy to play, and it doesn’t introduce some of the safety issues that a traditional dart game does.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Anywhere Darts - Double-Sided Dart Target Hangs Anywhere - Perfect for Kids and Families

text_fidelity_a:
Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops I've been using this for about two weeks now. It does what I bought it to do and I have a lot of fun using it, but there are certain flaws that lead me to say it's overpriced.

First the good: it's easy to put together and works as advertised. It took me a few tries to find the right fit (a little tighter than I first thought) and several practice attempts before I could get the weight spinning long enough for a good workout (but I was never that great at regular hula hoops as a kid). Playing with the length of the cord also resulted in a much better workout, and the catch is very strong; it holds whatever length I set no matter how hard or long I use it.

Snapping the links into position was moderately challenging, but my grip strength is relatively poor so no surprise there. Opening and closing the hoop for actual use is easy, and that's what's important. There's a novelty factor to this, of course, but I do find it fun to use, which motivates me to use it regularly.

Now the not so good: a few of the pieces arrived broken. Although I don't need those links now, it's disappointing that I won't have them in the future if need be.

A bigger issue is that this thing is loud -- not "wake the neighbors" loud but loud enough to disturb others in the house. I wasn't expecting it to be utterly silent, but neither was I expecting this rattling. This limits my use of it somewhat.

I got this as a cardio option other than walking or biking. I have posterior tibial tendonitis -- a fancy way of saying tendonitis of the ankle/foot; walking or running for long distances can irritate it, and biking isn't always an option for me. The weighted hula hoop is a very good alternative to these activities because I can get a good cardio workout without aggravating my PTT. Admittedly, I can't go as long with this as I can walking or biking, but I can make it a lot more intense. Besides, this is still kind of new to me, and I'm confident that I can build my stamina over time. Judging from the feel of the materials, though, I'm not sure how durable this device will be.

Prices here vary all the time, of course. I got this for about $35 altogether. Given the breakage, I'd say that was slightly overpriced; I certainly wouldn't advise anyone to pay more than that for this. It's a nice tool for your home gym, but I'd wait to buy it on sale or at least until February when most of us have left our new year's resolutions in the dust.
text_fidelity_b: Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops

Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1 I like this flashlight. It is made in China, but feels sturdier than the $10 generic non-rechargeable flashlights that I also see on Amazon. I trust the charging circuitry on an Energizer-branded flashlight more than on a generic flashlight (and the batteries in these flashlights are powerful enough that safe recharging is important). The flashlight has 3 brightness modes plus one flashing mode. I like that the strobe mode needs to be activated by a double-tap on the power button, so I am very unlikely to get that mode accidentally (and I hate flashlights that start strobing when I don't want them to). The steady mode has a nice wide uniform beam despite the flashlight having a compact size (1.2 inches at the widest). A lot of cheaper flashlights are bright only in the center, then fade rapidly towards the sides. I find the uniform beam to be much more useful.

Yes, the battery is not replaceable and the whole unit will have to be discarded when the battery no longer holds it charge. Hopefully that will be after hundreds of charges, which is many years for me and I'll probably lose the flashlight before that happens. If you use your flashlight for hours every day, then this may be a bigger concern to you.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1

text_fidelity_a:
Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit It’s like magic with a feeling of accomplishment. I don’t think I’ve ever glided before. Stand firm, lean and decide where to wander. It delivers pure delight. That’s the most important element that the Ninebot delivers.

The tech specs are available and don’t need repeating. If you’ve looked this far, you know what all the reviews say. The Ninebot is not the bone breaker ‘hover board’ of past years reputation. It’s a transport device. It’s something different. It’s powerful. It’s solid. The design incorporates a slew of bells and whistles connected and monitored through the smartphone.

Incorporated in the ‘system’ is enforced, demonstrated control teaching. New aspects of transport are unlocked as distance and demonstrated operational progress are accumulated on the Ninebot.

The first climb on board was easy. It is a noticeable step up. You feel the gyros. You sense the control variables. There’s more than I expected. Then I started to overthink. Mistake. Fast get off. The Ninebot is powerful and must be eased into.

I thought about it for a day. It needs respect. To be clear, you can hurt yourself. The step up is significant. The distance down and out of control is adequate for inducing unexpected orthopedic maneuvers.

You think it through again. Helmet? Check. Elbow and wrist support? Check. Watch the videos a few times for subtlety. Try again.

So, I mastered it without injury. I took my time. It’s a bicycle thing. You know it when you know it and you won’t forget.

The tech specs are well defined in the advertised representations. It feels bulkier to carry than the weight might indicat. I am most impressed with the blow-out design, the ‘system integration”, And the power … lots of power. Amazing.
text_fidelity_b: Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Im forced to take this 70$ loss, but I do not recommend these brakes if u have  any intentions of ever needing to take them apart for whatever reason. I don't see other reviews with this problem,  so its possible I have an error set, and they aren't all like this. But from a personal perspective, my experience is 100% dissatisfaction.  I'm beyond the return time frame. Lesson learned. Sometimes, even the good reviews can lead to a bad purchase. Unfortunately, I am ordering Shimano like my gut told me to from the beginning. text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp Everyone I know uses Black Diamond headlamps, but I've always owned Petzl. I've always wondered if I'd like BD better. When I had a bag stolen that had my newest Petzl headlamp in it I thought I'd try out the Black Diamond Revolt. For a headlamp that can recharge batteries with a USB cable it was a really good price, so I pulled the trigger on it. It has adequate lumens for my purposes (backpacking, evening hiking, and use around the house), although it isn't quite as bright as my similarly priced Petzl models. It has an awesome, fully adjustable dimmer setting that is the one thing that stands out as better than any other headlamp I've used. It also has a red LED setting, which is important to me - I actually find that I use the red LED way more than the white for late night use. As far as features go, I'm happy with everything you get with the Revolt.

The more I've used this headlamp though, I have a few minor complaints compared to similar offerings from Petzl. As mentioned above, I use the red LED setting often. It's great when you want to maintain night vision. I also like that if I wake up in the middle of the night and quickly use my lamp, the red LED wakes me up less than a bright white light. The problem for me is that the red setting on the Revolt is way too dim. It's hard to see anything that's more than just a few feet away. This makes it so that I can't use it in as many situations as I could with my old Petzl. I definitely wish it were brighter in the red mode.

Another feature on most headlamps is an adjustable angle setting where you can click it up and down to choose how high the lamp points. The Revolt has solid detents that seem like they will hold up well over time. This is kind of splitting hairs, but I don't like how widely spaced the detents are. It always seems to be too high or too low. YMMV, but I liked Petzl again here for the finer adjustments. I have to fiddle with the Revolt more often.

On the other hand, I'm not gentle with my headlamps. I use them constantly at home and work and any time I backpack or travel. I cram them into bags, toss them around a bit, bump them on things and occasionally drop them. It's hard to say, but friends that I work with and backpack with seem to have better luck with their Black Diamond lamps' durability. The Revolt is solidly built and seems to use batteries very efficiently. It seems like it might be a little sturdier and maybe last longer than my previous Petzl lamps, but that's purely a guess at this point. We'll see, but so far so good. I'm basing that more on friends' experiences with BD lamps. Either way, it's certainly no worse.

Overall, I think this is a pretty good headlamp. It's a solid value for the price and does everything I want it to. I'll continue to use it pretty happily, but when it comes time to replace it, I'll go back to Petzl. Even if the Revolt is a little sturdier, I like the way Petzl lamps work and feel. They're less clunky and they just seems to have their headlamps really dialed across the board. They're comfortable, intuitive and very well designed. Get a Revolt if you want a solid, functional headlamp, but get a Petzl if you really want to love it.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Revolt Headlamp

text_fidelity_a:
ust Heritage Lensatic Compass with Lightweight Brass Construction for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Hunting and Outdoor Survival This UST HERITAGE LENSATIC COMPASS is beautiful, with its liquid-filled needle capsule, and its polished brass case. It’s fairly heavy (4.7 oz.), so it may not be the best choice for backpacking, but it’s a great learning compass.

To use it, the first step is to hold it level, so that the needle swings freely without touching the sides of the capsule. The second step is to make sure there is no metal (e.g., a hunting knife) or magnetic field nearby, as either will affect the needle direction and prevent an accurate reading. The third step is to let the needle “settle” before you take your reading.

The box says there are complete instructions for use inside—NOT true, but the Ultimate Survival Technologies web site has an excellent one-page PDF that gives two methods for using the compass to sight distant objects and determine directions. “Lensatic” means that the compass has a prismatic lens for reading the outer (mils/milliradians) or inner (degrees) scales and determining the bearing or azimuth. This lens really works—it magnifies the scale figures.

The luminous directional letters and sighting lines also work. The “hanging loop” is actually a thumb loop that helps you steady the compass as you sight with it. My brass case has a few tiny nicks and pits on the bottom and on the lens pivot, but the brass cover is pristine and gorgeous. I polish the case with Brasso.

Once you have this compass, you can learn all about navigation. Start by looking up “Compass” on Wikipedia, and it will lead you to many fascinating online articles.
text_fidelity_b: ust Heritage Lensatic Compass with Lightweight Brass Construction for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Hunting and Outdoor Survival

CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover Camelback rarely disappoints and the quality of this bag is no exception. The back of it is soft and supportive against your back while offering comfort and air-flow that does not diminish when the bag and 3-liter bladder are full. The bag is durable and sturdy, with soft lining on some inner pockets for things like a cell phone, GPS, or satellite link. Inside there are larger compartments with a couple of smaller ones, and snack pockets on the waist-band (at least that's what I use them for!). There is also a built-in pocket for the rain shield so you won't lose it, as well as clips for your poles. We were even able to fit a small tent in the stash pocket! I never would have guessed the bag could have that capacity going by looks alone.

However, there are a couple of things I wish I could change about the bag. The water compartment is pretty big, it cuts into pack space more than I'd like when it's full. There also aren't many clips and loops on the outside beyond the pole clips. Not spaces for carabiners etc. Dirty shoes, dog bowls, they all have to go IN the pack.
